title: The algebras of the Giry monad: the adjunction with the Giry monad (Theorem 2)
author: Kirk Sturtz
work: The algebras of the Giry monad
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's main theorem (source0.tex lines 357-358), that the free/forgetful pair between measurable spaces and measurable convex spaces together with the unit and the natural transformation built from the E-operators forms an adjunction whose induced monad is the Giry monad. Its retained complete proof (lines 359-428) is a genuine 70-line categorical argument: the two triangular identities are verified by chasing elements through the article's own TikZ diagrams, using the affine-measurable-function lemma (delivered as context) to pass from a commutative triangle to a commutative square, pushing probability measures forward along non-affine measurable maps, and then identifying the induced monad with the Giry monad by re-deriving the multiplication from the E-operators. The residual difficulty is the construction of the comparison between the algebraic (convex-space) and measure-theoretic descriptions and the verification of the triangular identities for a monad on measurable spaces, which is research-level category theory rather than an ordinary PhD qualifying exercise.
